shortlist.title: OpenMobile-2 proves open-source smartphone agents can rival proprietary models
shortlist.summary: Smartphone agents don't get better by processing more data. They improve by training on as many different apps as possible. The researchers behind OpenMobile-2 built an open training environment with more than 110 applications, including 35 replicas of popular apps. On real Android devices, their model scores highest among open agents, the authors say. shortlist.raw_text: Existing vision-language models (VLMs) remain unreliable for fine-grained visual perception. In this report, we present WeVisOne-VL (WeChat Vision All-in-One), a powerful VLM that unifies object-level and pixel-level perception through structured next-token prediction. It supports multiple visual tasks including object detection, referring localization, counting, OCR, segmentation, and matting, enabling localization at any user-specific granularity, from points and boxes to masks and alpha mattes. Architecturally, we integrate a lightweight pixel decoder into the VLM via a special <OBJ> token to generate instance-level pixel outputs. We train the model with a three-stage curriculum SFT followed by mixed-task RL. Across over 30 benchmarks, WeVisOne-VL demonstrates leading performance on both object-level and pixel-level tasks, while maintaining robust rejection for object-absent queries. By releasing WeVisOne-VL to the open-source community, we hope to advance VLMs from broad visual understanding toward truly reliable perception systems for real-world deployment.

shortlist.raw_text: High-quality image editing requires precise modification of target regions while preserving the content of unrelated regions. Existing editing models produce flattened outputs that limit precise local manipulation and layer reuse, while decomposition methods typically optimize layer recovery separately from instruction-driven editing. To this end, we introduce LayerEditor, a unified framework that couples instruction-guided image editing with controllable generation of reusable RGBA layers. At its core, In-Context RGB-Alpha Token Modeling jointly represents the edited canvas and an ordered sequence of RGB-Alpha layers within a single token sequence, enabling semantic edits and explicit control over individual layer content. To retain the pretrained model's editing capability during adaptation to layered outputs, we propose Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation, which transfers its editing prior to both the edited canvas and the image composed from the predicted layers. To support training and evaluation, we construct LayerEditor-100K, a large-scale paired image-editing dataset with ordered RGBA layer annotations, and introduce dedicated benchmarks for layered editing. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LayerEditor maintains strong editing fidelity while generating accurate RGBA layers, supporting both flexible layer-level manipulation and multi-layer decomposition.

Title: OpenAI offers discounts up to 90 percent to poach Anthropic's biggest customers

Text:
OpenAI is poaching Anthropic's customers with steep discounts. Companies like Rippling, Replit, and DataCamp say they've cut AI costs by up to 90 percent after switching. Anthropic's growth has slowed, but OpenAI is trading its own margins for market share. Chinese rivals like Deepseek are piling on more price pressure. The article OpenAI offers discounts up to 90 percent to poach Anthropic's biggest customers appeared first on The Decoder .

Article text (excerpt):
OpenAI is reportedly pulling major customers away from Anthropic with aggressive discounts, and the strategy is working. Companies like Rippling, Replit, and DataCamp are shifting more of their AI spending to OpenAI, The Information reports . Rippling CEO Parker Conrad said his company boosted OpenAI's share of its coding workload from 16 to 52 percent, while Anthropic's share fell from 57 to 18 percent.
Replit switched after OpenAI offered more than 30 percent off a contract worth over $100 million a year. DataCamp CEO Jonathan Cornelissen said OpenAI's pricing cut his costs by 80 to 90 percent. A US bank with more than $7 billion in assets got its ChatGPT seats doubled to 500 employees at no extra charge, paying under $7 per user instead of the usual $20 or more.
OpenAI is partly buying market share at the expense of its own margins, but it has also achieved real price cuts through its Sol and Luna model lines thanks to more efficient models and infrastructure. Anthropic's growth slowed from Q2 to Q3 , according to an investor memo. Both companies also face growing price pressure from China, where new models by Deepseek and Kimi deliver comparable performance for a fraction of the cost. Ad Ad

Coverage from Cryptopolitan on MSN: "OpenAI cuts GPT-6 Sol and Luna prices by 50% to defend developer share"
On Tuesday, OpenAI introduced the GPT-6 Sol and the GPT-6 Luna, and they are both priced to be at least 50% lower than the rates of the GPT-5.6 models they supersede. OpenAI’s price cuts are aimed at ...

Coverage from Yahoo Finance: "OpenAI’s GPT-6 Sol and Luna Cut Prices 50% — and the Three-Tier Family Just Ended the Coordinated Slowdown"
OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol and Luna arrived on September 22, 2026 with permanent pricing that cuts API costs by 50 percent versus the GPT-5.6 series. Sol runs at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output; Luna at $0.10 and $0.50. Together with the existing Astra at $10 and $50, the company now fields a three-tier family covering the entire cost spectrum from enterprise-grade reasoning to high-volume clerical work. The pricing was confirmed as permanent, not promotional, by an OpenAI spokesperson speaking to VentureBeat .
What that structure means in practice is visible in the competitive comparison. Sol matches Grok 4.7's $2 input price and arrives the day after xAI's pricing undercut started the current war. It undercuts Anthropic's Opus 5.5, released ninety minutes earlier at $4/$20, on both input and output. Luna at $0.10/$0.50 sits below every frontier-class model on the market, including Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.6 Flash at $0.14/$0.28. A developer choosing between these models no longer leaves the OpenAI ecosystem regardless of budget.
The performance data tells a more complicated story than the pricing. On AutomationBench , Sol scores 33.2 percent at $0.27 per task, compared to Opus 5's 26.9 percent at roughly $3 per task. That is an 11x cost advantage for higher measured performance. On DeepSWE v1.1, the agentic coding benchmark, Sol reaches 68.8 percent and Luna 66.6 percent.
But Sol actually regressed on OSWorld 2.0, the computer-use benchmark, scoring 60.5 percent at xhigh effort versus GPT-5.6 Sol's 65.7 percent. A model that costs half as much performs worse on the broadest capability test. OpenAI is choosing to optimize for cost-per-task over capability ceiling – a decision that favors high-volume production workflows but leaves a gap for builders who need peak performance on complex, multi-step reasoning.
The alignment numbers are where the strategic bet becomes clear. OpenAI reports that GPT-6 Sol's coding deception rate dropped to 1.3 percent, down from 10.4 percent in GPT-5.6 Sol. Broken tool disclosure failure fell from 77.5 percent to 4.9 percent. These are the same kind of behavioral safety gains that Anthropic has built its brand around – and OpenAI is delivering them at a model priced at one-fifth of the frontier tier.

Background (Reddit API controversy, Wikipedia):
The Reddit API controversy was a dispute between Reddit and portions of its user and developer communities following Reddit's April 2023 announcement that it would begin charging for access to its API, which had previously been free. The changes affected third-party applications and raised concerns about the continued availability of moderation tools and accessibility applications.

Background (Free energy principle, Wikipedia):
The free energy principle is a mathematical principle of information physics. Its application to fMRI brain imaging data as a theoretical framework suggests that the brain reduces surprise or uncertainty by making predictions based on internal models and uses sensory input to update its models so as to improve the accuracy of its predictions. This principle approximates an integration of Bayesian inference with active inference, where sensory feedback refines prediction-guided actions. From it, wide-ranging inferences have been made about brain function, perception, and action. Its applicability to living systems has been questioned.

text:
OpenAI is offering 90 percent discounts to poach Anthropic’s biggest corporate clients.

Rippling slashed Anthropic's share of its coding workload from 57 percent down to 18.

Here is how the price war is working.

Replit shifted after OpenAI offered more than 30 percent off a contract worth over $100 million a year.

DataCamp CEO Jonathan Cornelissen said the move cut his company's costs by 80 to 90 percent.

A US bank with over $7 billion in assets got 500 ChatGPT seats for under $7 per user, down from the usual $20.

OpenAI isn't only losing margin to win market share. It is launching cheaper infrastructure.

The new GPT-6 Sol model costs $2 per million input tokens. That gives it an 11x cost advantage over Anthropic's Opus 5 on standard task benchmarks.

The cheap prices come with a catch:
• GPT-6 Sol regressed on OSWorld 2.0 computer-use tests
• Peak performance on complex multi-step reasoning is down
• China's Deepseek is applying matching price pressure from below

OpenAI chose to sacrifice capability ceilings for volume.

My read: enterprise AI is shifting from a capability race to a margin squeeze. Most companies will trade a bit of reasoning power for a 90 percent discount.

Would your company switch AI models if it cut your bill by 80 percent?

Source: The Decoder, with reporting from Cryptopolitan on MSN and Yahoo Finance
